Time Value of Money: Present Value, Future Value and Annuities

A rupee today is worth more than a rupee next year, because it can earn a return in the meantime and inflation erodes it. Almost all of finance rests on this idea, and this guide gives the formulas with worked numbers.

2 min readFor MBA, BBA and BBMUpdated 2 November 2026

Why money has time value

  • Opportunity: money today can be invested and earn a return.
  • Inflation: prices rise, so the same money buys less later.
  • Risk: a promise of future money may not be kept.

The formulas, worked at 10%

ConceptFormulaExampleAnswer
Future valuePV × (1 + r)^n₹10,000 for 5 years₹16,105
Present valueFV ÷ (1 + r)^n₹1,00,000 due in 5 years₹62,092
Future value of an annuityA × [(1 + r)^n − 1] ÷ r₹10,000 a year for 5 years₹61,051
Present value of an annuityA × [1 − (1 + r)^−n] ÷ r₹10,000 a year for 5 years₹37,908
Present value of a perpetuityA ÷ r₹10,000 a year forever₹1,00,000

Ordinary annuity and annuity due

In an ordinary annuity, payments are made at the end of each period, as with most loan EMIs. In an annuity due, they are made at the start, as with rent or insurance premiums. An annuity due is worth more, because each payment earns one extra period of return: its value equals the ordinary annuity's value × (1 + r).

Compounding frequency and effective rate

Effective annual rate = (1 + r/m)^m − 1. A 12% rate compounded monthly gives (1 + 0.01)^12 − 1 = 12.68%. Compounded yearly, it would be just 12%.

So when comparing a loan or deposit, compare effective rates and not just the stated rate.

Rule of 72

Divide 72 by the annual rate to estimate the years needed to double your money. At 8%, that is 72 ÷ 8 = 9 years. It is a shortcut for mental arithmetic, and is most accurate for rates between about 6% and 12%.

Where it is used

  • Capital budgeting: NPV and IRR discount future cash flows.
  • Bond pricing: a bond's price is the present value of its coupons and face value.
  • Valuation: a discounted cash flow valuation estimates a company's value from its future cash flows.
  • Loans: an EMI is the annuity payment that repays a loan.
  • Personal finance: SIP growth and retirement planning.

Exam and interview questions

What is the difference between compounding and discounting?

Compounding moves money forward, from a present value to a future value. Discounting moves money back, from a future value to a present value.

Why is present value lower than future value?

Because future money is discounted for the return you could have earned in the meantime, and for risk.

What is a perpetuity?

A stream of equal payments that goes on forever. Its present value is the payment divided by the discount rate.
